mod.overview: Tribal God 6.6 (Ultra_Tribal_God, by Dustin 'X-Ecutioner' Bruce, 2003) is a heavily expanded build of stock Tribes with four armor classes (Asassin, Mercenary, Engineer, BoRg), dozens of new weapons, psionic-style abilities, droids, a jail system and over twenty deployable turrets and structures. Armors carry 10 to 20 weapons instead of 3 to 5, players choose a class and spawn with a large loadout, and stock placement rules are replaced by a 'fair play' check that keeps deployables near friendly objects and away from enemy bases.
notes: Four armor classes: Asassin (larmor/lfemale), Mercenary (marmor/mfemale), Engineer (one Earmor suit for both genders) and BoRg (harmor). Weapon slots ($MaxWeapons): male Asassin 20, female Asassin 15, Mercenary 12, Engineer 10, BoRg 10 (stock 3/4/5).

Players pick a spawn class in the Character Options menu (Light, Medium, Engineer, Heavy, saved favorites or random); game.cs buys the class's $spawnBuyList through buyItem, so carry limits apply. Default starting weapons: Asassin Double Plasma, Mercenary Tank Shredder, Engineer Plasma Cannon, BoRg Tank RPG.
Spawn protection sets the player's shieldStrength to 1500 for $TG::SafeSpawnTime seconds (1.75 by default).

Placement: turrets and the Portable Hole deploy through deployable() in deployableFuncts.cs, which allows any surface within 4 m at any angle with no spacing or per-area turret count. It refuses only when the player is jailed, the team limit is reached, or an enemy inventory station, ammo station, turret or generator is inside a 300 m box (god admins exempt). Its proximity and 'objects in the way' checks call CountObjects(set, ""), which only matches objects with an empty datablock name, so they never block.

Most other deployables need a friendly static object within a box around the aim point (150 m for doors, ammo station, motion sensor, Huge Wall and teleport; 999 m for the inventory station). TG::CheckFairPlay, used by the Deployable Base and IBlock, refuses if any non-friendly static, including neutral mission objects, is in the box.

Every deployable() deploy adds $TG::FlagDefencePoints (1 by default) to the deployer's score with a 'Defending Your Flag' message, wherever it is placed; the message prints scoreKills for both DeathCount and Kill Count. The deployer is made the owner of the turret for kill credit, except for the Nuclear Turret.
The Asassin can carry only a few deployables (Decoy Carrier, Probe Droid, Cloak Droid, Clone, Portable Hole, blast door) but every turret pack; all turret packs are carried by every armor.

Player damage is $DamageScale[armor, type] x damage. Damage types with no DamageScale entry (Jail, Nuker, Claymor, Debug, Misc, Admin) do no normal health damage to players; Player::onDamage gives several types special effects instead (EMP, Claymor and Flash drain energy or drop items, Nuker strips enemies and heals teammates, Smoke adds 0.25 directly). Enemy head hits with the Bullet or LiL POO mkii types gib the target for triple damage.
Shield packs absorb energy x shieldStrength, at 0.75x strength against shrapnel and mortar. The packs cost about 0.1 energy per second while running (stock 9 to 10).

Infinite-ammo switches in TribalPrefs.cs: only Double Plasma, Mine Launcher, Mortar and Tank Shredder read their weapon setting; $TG::InfiniteAmmo:DiscLauncher and :RepairKit are never read. Grenade::onUse uses a grenade only when $TG::InfiniteAmmo:Grens is true, the reverse of its meaning, and LiLBoost reads the Grens setting instead of Boosts. $TG::InfiniteDropAmmo makes dropped ammo free.
Weapon modes for the Mine Launcher, Mortar, Blaster and Disc Launcher are chosen in the Tab menu under Character Options > Weapon Options.
$TG::GiveallOn (off by default) enables the giveall refill for admins, the chat word HOOKITUPX (a refill for any player) and QUADDISC (the hidden Quad Disc).

Admin system with God, Super Admin and Public Admin levels set by passwords in TribalPrefs.cs, plus optional voting for Public Admin. With $TG::LogIps on, joiners' addresses and names are logged to config\IpLoggs.cs, admins are told when an address uses a new name, and the fourth different name from one address is kicked.

Several team counts (Jail Capture Pad, IBlock, Air Base, Freezing Pad) are never lowered when the object is destroyed and are not reset between missions, so those limits fill up for the rest of the server session.

JailPack.summary: Builds a team jail cell high in the air above the deployer: force-field and blast-wall panels, a prisoner pad inside, a team-only door and a release pad on the roof. Enemies captured by Jail Capture Pads are teleported into it.
notes: One jail per team (limit key JailPackage). The count is only reset by Mission::reinitData; destroying the jail does not decrement it.

Built relative to the deployer's own position, not the aim point, and not rotated to their facing: panels sit about 80 to 86 units above the deployer. The deploy message says 250m, but the code offsets are about 80 to 86.

Fair-play check over static objects in a 350-unit box: refused if the box holds only non-friendly objects (neutral mission objects count as non-friendly) or no objects at all; allowed if any friendly object is present.
The cell door (Jail::JailDoorShape) opens only for the jail team: it rises 6 units and fades out, then closes after 2.5 seconds. It explodes with radius damage when destroyed.

The prisoner pad (jailStand) only prints 'No Escape This Way'. Prisoners are released by a schedule set when they are jailed: after 30 seconds, a prisoner within 10 units of the jail team's roof release pad is moved onto it.
Stepping on the roof release pad announces the player as paroled. Standing on it repeatedly builds a counter: at 5 and 10 the player is shoved off with an impulse.
Destroying the prisoner pad (maxDamage 20000) deletes all 14 jail pieces.

Bug: the jail pieces are tracked in global variables $JailSide1 to $JailSide14, so a second team's jail overwrites the first's references, and destroying either prisoner pad deletes the most recently built jail.
Bug: the out-of-mission-area message is sent to %client before it is assigned, so the player gets no message; jailStand::onCollision centerprints to an undefined %client.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

JailCapPack.summary: Deploys a small pad that teleports any enemy who steps on it into the deploying team's Jail Cell for 30 seconds.
notes: Cannot be deployed within 10 units of the team's own flag. There is no fair-play or surface check.

An enemy who touches the pad is moved to the prisoner pad of every jail not owned by their team (the last one found wins). For 30 seconds they cannot suicide, and the deploy code that most turrets use (deployable()) and the Portable Hole refuse to deploy for them.
Teammates who touch it just get a message. If no enemy jail exists, the victim is not moved, but a 'prison' message is still broadcast to everyone.
The pad is not used up and has no working cooldown: the recharge branch checks %this.disabled, which nothing ever sets.
No destroy handler decrements the team count and Mission::reinitData does not reset it, so the team limit of 25 counts every pad deployed during the server session.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

hugewall.summary: Raises a large wall of blast-door panels in front of the deployer: a grid four panels wide and three high, facing the way the deployer looks.
notes: Placed relative to the deployer's position and rotation, not the aim point. There is no surface or line-of-sight requirement.
Requires a friendly static object within a 150-unit box of the aim point, and the deployer must be more than 5 units from their own flag.

Each panel (HugeWallShape) has 20000 maxDamage. Its onDamage tries to stop team damage from pushing a panel past its disabled level, but it overwrites the capped value right away, so the cap has no effect.
HugeWallShape::onDestroyed is empty: no explosion and no count decrement. The team limit of 2 is only reset by Mission::reinitData.
Bug: 13 panels are created but only 12 are positioned. objSide5 is never given a position or team.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

Deployablebase.summary: Builds a complete small base around the deployer in one go: force-field walls, blast-wall ceiling, two team-only doors, two Inventory Stations, a Command Station, two Plasma Turrets on the roof, a floating-pad floor and a generator.
notes: One per team. Built at fixed offsets from the deployer's position, axis-aligned, regardless of facing, aim or surface.

Fair-play check (TG::CheckFairPlay) over static objects in a 175-unit box around the deployer: there must be at least one friendly object and no non-friendly ones. Neutral mission objects count as non-friendly.
The doors open only for teammates: they move up 6 units and return after 2 seconds. Fliers that hit a door take 0.01 damage.
The generator is placed 5109 units below the deployer, effectively underground.
Collapse rule: deploying sets a global counter to 5. Each destroyed force-field wall or door (6 pieces in total) lowers it, and at 0 every piece of the base is deleted and the team count is freed.

Bug: the counter ($DplBase::EnabledCnt) and the piece list ($BaseObj0 to $BaseObj16) are global, not per base. A second team's base resets the counter and overwrites the list, so destroying pieces of either base can delete the newest one.
The force-field walls and doors have 20000 maxDamage. Their onDamage has the same ineffective team-damage cap as the Huge Wall.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

DecoyCarrier.summary: Deploys a fake flag carrier in front of the deployer: a light-armor hologram holding a decoy flag and a decoy sniper rifle, labelled with the deployer's name.
notes: Placed 2.5 units in front of the deployer, using their rotation. There is no surface, area or fair-play check.
The figure is a Hologram1 shape (light armor model). The decoy flag (Flag101) and decoy weapon (DecoyWeapon) are separate fragile shapes.

Bug: the deploy count is incremented for the team of an undefined %sensor rather than the deployer's team, so the team limit of 5 never fills. Meanwhile the flag and weapon each decrement the team's DecoyCarrier count when destroyed, and the figure decrements the Hologram count, which lets the team exceed its hologram limit.
Usable by every armor, including Asassin.
DecoyCarrier.source: deployableCarrier.cs DecoyCarrier::deployshape; staticshape.cs Flag101::onDestroyed, DecoyWeapon::onDestroyed, Hologram1::onDestroyed

IBlock.summary: Places a very large floor interior (iblock.dis) just under the deployer's feet, giving a huge platform to build on.
notes: Placed 1.5 units below the deployer and turned to their facing.

Fair-play check (TG::CheckFairPlay) over static objects in a 200-unit box around the deployer: there must be at least one friendly object and no non-friendly ones (neutral objects count as non-friendly).
Cannot be deployed within 50 units of the team's own flag.

One per team. The floor is an InteriorShape with no destroy handler, and its count is only reset when the script is first executed (Mission::reinitData does not include it), so a team gets one for the whole server session.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

AirBasePack.summary: Builds a floating air base 150 units straight above the deployer: floor and roof pads, force-field walls, a Vehicle Station and Vehicle Pad, an Inventory Station, a Command Station, a Medium Pulse Sensor and two Solar Panels.
notes: The aim point must be terrain, and the deployer must be at least 50 units from their own flag.
The force-field walls have 50000 maxDamage.
The stations, sensor and panels are registered with NukeList, which tags them for the admin 'neutron bomb' deployable cleanup.

The team limit is 2, but nothing ever lowers or resets the AirBasePack count. The file's reset loop indexes with the wrong variable, Mission::reinitData resets an 'airbase' key instead, and the only 'airbase' decrement (ABPortGenerator::onDestroyed) is defined inside another function. So each team gets 2 for the server session.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.
AirBasePack.source: deployableAirBase.cs AirBasePack::deployshape; staticshape.cs LargeRadar::onDestroyed; AdminFunctions.cs NukeList

BlastWall.summary: Deploys a single blast-door panel at the aim point, turned to the deployer's facing.
notes: Only needs a target within 3 units. There is no surface, area or fair-play check, so it can be placed against anything.
Destroying it decrements the team count.
Bug: the limit check uses > instead of >=, so a team can deploy 11 against the limit of 10.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

lgaForceFieldPack.summary: Deploys the largest team force-field door (4x17 panel). It opens briefly for teammates and punishes enemies who touch it.
notes: Placed at the aim point within 3 units, upright and facing the deployer's rotation.
Requires a friendly static object within a 150-unit box of the aim point.
A teammate touching it makes the field fade out and rise 6 units, then return after 1 second.

An enemy touching it loses 30 energy, gets a damage flash and is knocked back, and their damage level is set to 0.4. Because the level is set rather than added, an enemy with more than 0.4 damage is actually healed to 0.4.
Explodes with radius damage when destroyed.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

lgbForceFieldPack.summary: Deploys a large team force-field door (4x14 panel) that opens briefly for teammates and blocks everyone else.
notes: Placed at the aim point within 3 units, upright and facing the deployer's rotation.
Requires a friendly static object within a 150-unit box of the aim point.
A teammate touching it makes the field fade out and rise 6 units, then return after 1 second. Enemies are ignored.
Explodes with radius damage when destroyed.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

medaForceFieldPack.summary: Deploys a medium team force-field door (4x8 panel) that opens briefly for teammates and blocks everyone else.
notes: Placed at the aim point within 3 units, upright and facing the deployer's rotation.
Requires a friendly static object within a 150-unit box of the aim point.
A teammate touching it makes the field fade out and rise 6 units, then return after 1 second. Enemies are ignored.
Explodes with radius damage when destroyed.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

medbForceFieldPack.summary: Deploys a square team force-field door (5x5 panel) that opens briefly for teammates and blocks everyone else.
notes: Placed at the aim point within 3 units, upright and facing the deployer's rotation.
Requires a friendly static object within a 150-unit box of the aim point.
A teammate touching it makes the field fade out and rise 6 units, then return after 1 second. Enemies are ignored.
Explodes with radius damage when destroyed.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

medcForceFieldPack.summary: Deploys the smallest team force-field door (3x4 panel) that opens briefly for teammates and blocks everyone else.
notes: Placed at the aim point within 3 units, upright and facing the deployer's rotation.
Requires a friendly static object within a 150-unit box of the aim point.
A teammate touching it makes the field fade out and rise 6 units, then return after 1 second. Enemies are ignored.
Explodes with radius damage when destroyed.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

FlyerPack.summary: Deploys a small remote-controlled flier (NLAPC, an LAPC hull that fires fireballs). The player flies it directly while their body stays behind.
notes: The flier spawns at the aim point within 10 units, and control switches to it immediately.

One per team, and a player cannot run it while they already control a droid. In either refused case the pack is removed, and the script tries to give a Repair Pack by calling buyItem() with the player object instead of a client.
The deployer's body is left standing and unprotected.
The flier starts with full health and no energy, then recharges energy quickly.
The kill key (or the deployer's death) calls FlyerPack::onDestroyed, which returns control to the body and frees the team slot.
When the flier itself is destroyed, only the generic Vehicle::onDestroyed runs. FlyerPack::onDestroyed is not called by the engine, because the flier's datablock is NLAPC.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.
FlyerPack.source: deployableFlyer.cs FlyerPack::onDeploy, DeployFlyerPack, FlyerPack::onDestroyed; RemoteClientFuncts.cs remoteKill; vehicleFuncts.cs Vehicle::onDestroyed

HolePack.summary: Deploys a team-only portal panel that teammates can phase through. On a floor it drops them 4 units down; on walls it pushes them 4 units through.
notes: Uses the shared deployable() routine with no surface, flatness, area or fair-play checks and a 5-unit range. It can go on terrain, buildings or deployables at any angle, oriented to the surface.

A teammate touching it takes a tiny 0.01 'portal' damage, which Player::onDamage turns into a teleport. On a flat-floor portal (no X rotation), the player moves 4 units down. Depending on the portal's other rotation values, they move either 4 units up or 4 units along the portal's facing.
Enemies are not affected by it.
On deploy, the deployer's team hears 'Friendly Portal Deployed' and the enemy hears 'Hull Breech!'. The deployer gets 2 points plus the deployable() point award.
Jailed players cannot deploy it.
Usable by every armor.
HolePack.source: deployableHole.cs HolePack::deployShape, Portal::onCollision/onDestroyed; player.cs Player::onDamage ($TrapDam1 branch); deployableFuncts.cs deployable

ProbeDroidPack.summary: Launches a tiny camera-shaped flying probe from the deployer's muzzle and hands them control of it for scouting. It fires small fusion bolts.
notes: Two per team. Control switches to the probe immediately, and the deployer's body is left standing and unprotected.
Pressing jump ends the probe and returns control to the body.
Flying the probe into an enemy player just ends it. Flying it into a teammate kills the deployer.
The probe is very fragile. Destroying it returns control to the body and frees the team slot.
Usable by every armor.

CloakDroidPack.summary: Uploads the player into a cloaked Mercenary-armor droid body armed with a double plasma gun, while their real body waits behind under a strong energy shield.
notes: The droid spawns at the aim point within 10 units. The player watches from an observer camera for a 10-second upload countdown, then takes control.
The droid fades out (it is invisible) and has sensor suppression.

The droid's loadout: Plasma Gun, Double Plasma, LiLPOOMki, LiLPOOMkii, Disc Launcher, Mortar, Beacons, Grenades, Repair Kits and a Hack Pack. Weapons and ammo are set to the deployer's armor limits, not the droid's; non-weapon items are set to 999.
While the droid is active, the real body's shieldStrength is set to 9999, so its energy absorbs damage.
Pressing the kill key (after the upload finishes), or the droid being killed, returns control to the body. The droid is then removed after 5 seconds.
Five per team. A player cannot run two droids at once.
Backpack items in the loadout, and the Repair Pack given when the deploy is refused, are handed out through buyItem() called with a player object instead of a client.
Only Asassin and Engineer armors can carry it.
CloakDroidPack.source: droidCloakDroid.cs DeployCloakDroid, CloakDroidPack::onDestroyed; RemoteClientFuncts.cs remoteKill; game.cs Client::onKilled; player.cs shield absorption

ClonePack.summary: Uploads the player into a visible Mercenary-armor clone body loaded with heavy weapons, while their real body waits behind under a strong energy shield.
notes: The clone spawns at the aim point within 10 units. The player orbits it with the observer camera during a 10-second upload, then takes control.

The clone's loadout: TRocketLauncher, Double Plasma, LiLPOOMki, LiLPOOMkii, Disc Launcher, Mortar, Beacons, Grenades, Repair Kits, LiLFFB and a Repair Pack. Weapons and ammo use the deployer's armor limits; non-weapon items are set to 999.
Unlike the Cloak Droid, it is not cloaked and has no sensor suppression.
While the clone is active, the real body's shieldStrength is set to 9999, so its energy absorbs damage.
Pressing the kill key (after the upload finishes), or the clone being killed, returns control to the body. The clone is then removed after 5 seconds.
Three per team. A player cannot run two droids at once.
Usable by every armor.
ClonePack.source: droidCloneDroid.cs DeployClone, Clone::onDestroyed; RemoteClientFuncts.cs remoteKill; game.cs Client::onKilled

TeleportPack.summary: Deploys a team teleport pad, marked by an electrical beam. A teammate stepping on it is sent to another of the team's pads, and both pads then recharge for 5 seconds.
notes: Needs a flat spot on terrain, a building or a static shape within 3 units. The pad sits 1 unit above the aim point.
A teammate goes to the first other team pad in the global pad list, not to a chosen partner, so with three or more pads the destination is fixed.
Mercenary (male model only, marmor) and BoRg armors cannot teleport. The check misses the female Mercenary model (mfemale).
Each teleport has a 1 in 55 chance of dealing 0.15 crush damage to a non-admin player. Bug: in that case the 5-second re-enable is never scheduled, so both pads stay disabled for good.
When a pad is destroyed, it deals 20 debris damage to one other friendly pad, enough to destroy it, which can set off a chain.
Bug: the limit check reads the TeleportPack count, but deploying and destroying change the DeployableTeleport count, so the team limit of 2 is never reached.
Bug: a failed fair-play check (no friendly static object within a 150-unit box) only prints a warning and does not stop the deploy.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

HoloPack.summary: Deploys a stationary hologram of a player in armor, to draw fire or fake a defender.
notes: Needs a flat surface within 3 units and a clear area. It faces the deployer's rotation.
The model is random: light armor 30% of the time, medium 40% and heavy 30% (Hologram1, 2 and 3).
Team limit of 5 (key 'hologram'). Destroying a hologram frees a slot. Decoy Carrier figures also lower this count when destroyed, though they never raise it.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.

DeployableInvPack.summary: Deploys a remote inventory station so the team can re-equip in the field.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes, the range is 5 units instead of 3, and it can be placed on static shapes and turrets as well as terrain and buildings. There is no clear-area check, so it can overlap players and items.
New fair-play rule: there must be a friendly static object within a 999-unit box of the aim point, which in practice is almost anywhere on a map where the team owns something.
Must still be on a flat surface.
The station's map name is set to 'Inventory Station'; in stock Tribes it was left blank.
Medium, heavy (BoRg) and Engineer armors only.

DeployableAmmoPack.summary: Deploys a remote ammo station for restocking in the field.
notes: Same placement rules as stock Tribes (flat terrain or building within 3 units, clear area), plus a new fair-play rule: there must be a friendly static object within a 150-unit box of the aim point.
Medium, heavy (BoRg) and Engineer armors only.

MotionSensorPack.summary: Deploys a small motion sensor that detects moving enemies nearby. It can be stuck on floors, walls or ceilings.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes, it can also be placed on static shapes and turrets, and there is no clear-area check.
New fair-play rule: there must be a friendly static object within a 150-unit box of the aim point.
The deployer gets 2 points as soon as there is a valid target in range, before the fair-play and surface checks. Failed attempts still award the points, and they can be repeated.
Unlike stock Tribes, where light armor could carry one, it is not usable by the Asassin armor.

FreezePack.summary: Deploys an invisible trap pad that freezes any enemy who steps on it, switching their view to an observer camera so they cannot act.
notes: Needs only a target within 3 units. There is no surface or fair-play check. The pad fades out on deploy and is not visible to sensors.
An enemy who steps on it is frozen: control moves to an observer camera orbiting their body, and suicide is blocked. The pad schedules the release 10 seconds later.
Freeze() also schedules its own release using $TG::FreezePadTime, which no script in the mod defines, so that release is scheduled with an empty delay.
Teammates who step on it just get a message.
The pad has no destroy handler, and Mission::reinitData does not reset its count, so the team limit of 10 covers the whole server session.
Not usable by the Asassin armor.
FreezePack.source: deployableFreeze-KillPad.cs FreezePack::deployShape; staticshape.cs FreezePad::onCollision; AdminFunctions.cs Freeze, FreezeCheck

RailTurret.summary: Deploys a self-powered hellfire-gun turret that fires a rail laser beam at enemies: slow (one shot per 5 seconds) but long-ranged and tough.
notes: Placed with the mod's shared turret routine: aim within 4 m at any surface or object, at any angle (the turret is oriented to the surface). There is no flat-surface, clear-space or spacing check. Deployment is refused while jailed, or if any enemy inventory or ammo station, turret or generator lies inside a 300x300x300 m box around the spot (god admins exempt).
Fires railLaser, a laser beam with the sniper damage type that stays visible for 1.5 seconds.
Its own destroyed handler sets off a much larger debris blast than other turrets (fixed 20 m radius, 1.1 to 2.5 damage, against 3 to 9 m and 0.1 to 0.4 for the shared turret blast).
TeamItemMax.cs sets the team limit twice, first to 2 and then to 5; the later value of 5 applies.
It recharges at 20 when placed but at 8 after being re-enabled from a disabled state.
Its deployShape calls deployable() without returning the result, so onDeploy's Player::decItemCount never runs: the pack is not used up by deploying, and only the team limit stops repeat deploys.
RailTurret.source: turretRail.cs RailTurret::deployShape, DeployableRail::onAdd/onEnabled/onDestroyed; deployableFuncts.cs deployable(); Laser-LightningData.cs railLaser; TeamItemMax.cs

LaserTurretPack.summary: Deploys a remote turret that fires rapid, short laser pulses at enemies.
notes: Uses the shared turret placement rules: any surface within 4 m, no flat-surface or spacing check, blocked near enemy stations, turrets or generators (300 m box).
Fires LaserTrtLaser every 0.25 seconds. Being laser damage, head hits deal 30% extra (against BoRg armor only on the centre of the head).
Can be remotely controlled from a command station without base power, and can be taken over with the Hack Gun ($Hackable[LaserTurret]).
Its deployShape calls deployable() without returning the result, so onDeploy's Player::decItemCount never runs: the pack is not used up by deploying, and only the team limit stops repeat deploys.
LaserTurretPack.source: turretLaser.cs LaserTurretPack::deployShape, LaserTurret::onAdd/onDestroyed; deployableFuncts.cs deployable(); Laser-LightningData.cs LaserTrtLaser; player.cs Player::onDamage, Client::takeControl; packHackPack.cs

TurretPack.summary: Renamed Ion Turret: the stock remote turret, still firing small energy bolts, but with far longer range, more health and faster fire.
notes: Unlike stock, any armor, including the Assassin, can carry one (stock allowed medium and heavy only), and the team limit is 5 instead of 10.
Unlike stock, range rises from 30 to 135, health from 0.65 to 1, reload falls from 0.4 to 0.25 seconds and each shot costs less energy. It still fires MiniFusionBolt.

Unlike stock, placement uses the mod's shared routine: any surface or object within 4 m (stock 3 m) at any angle. The stock checks for terrain or buildings, flat ground, a clear 1 m spot, at most 2 turrets in a 50x50x25 m area and 10 m spacing are all gone. Instead deployment is refused while jailed or if any enemy inventory or ammo station, turret or generator lies inside a 300x300x300 m box (god admins exempt).
The deployer is set as the turret's owner, the step stock had commented out to give turret kills to the deployer, and earns $TG::FlagDefencePoints score for deploying it.
Like stock, it ignores base power and can be controlled from a command station without power.
Its deployShape calls deployable() without returning the result, so onDeploy's Player::decItemCount never runs: the pack is not used up by deploying, and only the team limit stops repeat deploys.
TurretPack.source: turretIon.cs TurretPack::deployShape, DeployableTurret; deployableFuncts.cs deployable(); turretFuncts.cs ItemMax; base item.cs TurretPack::deployShape

LaserTurretBPack.summary: Mini-Plasma Turret: a remote turret that lobs plasma bolts with a small blast radius.
notes: Uses the shared turret placement rules: any surface within 4 m, no flat-surface or spacing check, blocked near enemy stations, turrets or generators (300 m box).
Fires PlasmaBolt (plasma damage, 4 m blast) every 0.5 seconds.
Can be remotely controlled from a command station without base power, and can be taken over with the Hack Gun ($Hackable[LaserTurretB]).
Its deployShape calls deployable() without returning the result, so onDeploy's Player::decItemCount never runs: the pack is not used up by deploying, and only the team limit stops repeat deploys.
LaserTurretBPack.source: turretMini-Plasma.cs LaserTurretBPack::deployShape, LaserTurretB; deployableFuncts.cs deployable(); BulletData.cs PlasmaBolt; player.cs Client::takeControl; packHackPack.cs

FireBallTurretPack.summary: Deploys a remote turret that sprays exploding fireballs, ten per second, each with a wide blast.
notes: Uses the shared turret placement rules: any surface within 4 m, no flat-surface or spacing check, blocked near enemy stations, turrets or generators (300 m box).
Fires Fireball: a plasma-bolt-shaped shot with a fireball explosion, shrapnel damage type and a 15 m blast radius, every 0.1 seconds.
Shrapnel damage gets past energy shields more easily: Player::onDamage cuts shield strength to 75% against it.
Its deployShape calls deployable() without returning the result, so onDeploy's Player::decItemCount never runs: the pack is not used up by deploying, and only the team limit stops repeat deploys.
FireBallTurretPack.source: turretFireBall.cs FireBallTurretPack::deployShape, DeployableFireBall; deployableFuncts.cs deployable(); BulletData.cs Fireball; player.cs Player::onDamage

FlameTurretPack.summary: Deploys a short-range turret that pours out a near-continuous stream of slow flame shots.
notes: Uses the shared turret placement rules: any surface within 4 m, no flat-surface or spacing check, blocked near enemy stations, turrets or generators (300 m box).
Fires FlameLarge, a slow flame rocket with a 2 m blast and the flame damage type, every 0.02 seconds out to 45 m. It cannot be jammed (supressable = false).
Flame damage is scaled by armor: 2.5x against Engineer armor, 1.1x against BoRg, 0.9x against Assassin and 1.0x against Mercenary.
FlameTurret::onDestroyed also damages %this.cyl, a field that is never set, so that line does nothing.
Its deployShape calls deployable() without returning the result, so onDeploy's Player::decItemCount never runs: the pack is not used up by deploying, and only the team limit stops repeat deploys.

MiniSAMTurretPack.summary: Mini-S.A.M Turret: a missile turret that launches slow, long-lived seeking missiles at long range.
notes: Uses the shared turret placement rules: any surface within 4 m, no flat-surface or spacing check, blocked near enemy stations, turrets or generators (300 m box).
Fires MiniSAMproj, a seeking missile that starts slowly but stays alive for 20 seconds, with a 9.5 m blast, every 4 seconds.
It has no verifyTarget filter, unlike the mod's base Rocket Turret, which only fires at targets with a heat factor of 0.5 or more.
Can be remotely controlled from a command station without base power.
Its deployShape calls deployable() without returning the result, so onDeploy's Player::decItemCount never runs: the pack is not used up by deploying, and only the team limit stops repeat deploys.

NuclearTurretPack.summary: Deploys a mortar-type turret that lobs nuclear shells with a 500 m blast radius, which strip enemies of their gear and energy. One per team.
notes: Uses the shared turret placement rules: any surface within 4 m, no flat-surface or spacing check, blocked near enemy stations, turrets or generators (300 m box).
Fires MortarShellNuke, a grenade-type shell with the nuke damage type, every 5 seconds. It cannot be jammed.
When the nuke damage type hits an enemy player, they drop their weapon, pack and flag, their energy is emptied and their energy recharge stops for 10 seconds (it then returns at a raised rate).
Players wearing an active Engineer Pack are immune (isUnNukable). A player on the shooter's team is fully healed instead of damaged.
The handler also tries to add half the victim's health as damage, but it reads %this.maxDamage, a field that is never set on players, so this adds nothing.

Unlike the other turrets from the shared routine, the deployer is deliberately not set as owner, so kills are not credited to them. Which team the handler then treats as the shooter's was not determined from scripts.
Its deployShape calls deployable() without returning the result, so onDeploy's Player::decItemCount never runs: the pack is not used up by deploying, and only the team limit stops repeat deploys.

MiniELFTurretPack.summary: Mini-ELF Turret: a short-range lightning turret that drains enemy energy and makes them drop their weapon and pack.
notes: Uses the shared turret placement rules: any surface within 4 m, no flat-surface or spacing check, blocked near enemy stations, turrets or generators (300 m box).
Fires MiniELFTurretproj, a wide-cone (35 degree) lightning beam that drains 1000 energy per second and does very little damage, out to 50 m.
Its damage handler skips teammates unless team damage scale is 1. Each hit on a player applies the Mini-ELF damage type, which makes them drop their mounted weapon and pack.
Can be remotely controlled from a command station without base power.

MiniSmokeTurretPack.summary: Mini-Beam Of Pain: a short-range turret firing a thick, weak lightning beam.
notes: Uses the shared turret placement rules: any surface within 4 m, no flat-surface or spacing check, blocked near enemy stations, turrets or generators (300 m box).
Fires MiniSmokeTurretproj, a wide (beam width 2) lightning bolt with tiny damage and a 2 energy per second drain, out to 55 m.

The beam names the Mini-ELF damage type, but no MiniSmokeTurretproj::damageTarget exists, so hits go through the generic Lightning::damageTarget. That handler applies electricity damage, so the beam neither strips items like the Mini-ELF nor pushes and disarms like the Beam Of Pain weapon (BeamOfPainProj).
Can be remotely controlled from a command station without base power.

notes: Uses the shared turret placement rules: any surface within 4 m, no flat-surface or spacing check, blocked near enemy stations, turrets or generators (300 m box).
Fires TaserTrtCLaser every 0.1 seconds. Its damage conversion is 0.0001, so hits deal almost nothing. It has 10 health, recharges at 20 and can be jammed.

RTurretGenPack.summary: Deploys a portable generator that a Repair Turret needs nearby, both to be deployed and to keep repairing. One per team.
notes: Sold under Other Deployables. It must be placed within the mission boundaries, within 3 m, on flat terrain or a building with a clear 1 m spot. It does not use the shared turret routine or its enemy-proximity check.

The generator is marked RTurretPower. Repair Turret deployment looks for any such object, of any team, within a 30x30x30 m box, and its repair loop keeps running only while one is within its 150 m box.

When destroyed, it decrements the team count and tells the owning team it was lost. Its onDestroyed replaces the generic generator handler, so there is no debris blast, and it never clears RTurretPower, so a destroyed generator still counts as a power source.
As a Generator-class object, it blocks enemy turret deployment within the 300 m box.

RepairTurretPack.summary: Deploys a non-firing repair turret that fully repairs every friendly object near it every 10 seconds and heals any player who touches it. It needs a RepairTurret Gen within 30 m when deployed.
notes: Placement: within 3 m on terrain or a building, at any angle, with a clear 1 m spot. (It compares the object type against DeployablePlatform, which never matches, so platforms do not count.)

Deploying first looks for a RepairTurret Gen of any team in a 30x30x30 m box. The player's view switches to an orbit camera for 5 seconds before the turret appears or 'No RepairTurret Gen Was Found' is shown.
The pack is removed 5 seconds after any deploy attempt that passes the placement checks, even when no generator was found and nothing appears.
The deploy position and rotation are kept in shared globals ($RepPos, $RepRot), so two players deploying within the same 5 seconds can overwrite each other's spot.

Every 10 seconds it removes 5.0 damage (a full repair) from every same-team player, structure, vehicle and mine in a 150x150x150 m box. The loop starts from onEnabled and stops when no RTurretPower object is left in that box.
Touching it fully heals any living player. onCollision reads both teams but never compares them, so enemies are healed too.

Every 60 seconds after deployment, its damage is set to half its remaining health, which pulls it toward about one-third damaged. The loop stops, with a team warning, once the turret is no longer enabled.
On destruction it alerts both teams. It clears RTurretPower on itself, not on its generator.

ObeliskPack.summary: Obelisk of Light: a tall tower with a laser gun on top that fires a heavy beam out to 350 m. It must be deployed next to an unused Obelisk Power Source. One per team.
notes: Placement: within 3 m on a flat surface that is not a building interior, with a clear 1 m spot, and within a 70x70x50 m box of an Obelisk Power Source not yet linked to an obelisk. The power source's team is not checked, so an enemy's unused one also works. It does not use the shared turret routine or its enemy-proximity check.

Two objects are created: the tower (ObeliskOfLight, a decoration shape) and the gun (RealObeliskOfLight) 11.5 m above it. The gun fires ObeliskBeam and does not need line of sight to track (castLOS = false).
The gun needs 80 energy per shot, all of its energy, so recharge rather than its 2-second reload sets the firing rate.

Destroying the tower also destroys the gun, frees the power source and decrements the team count. Destroying only the gun does none of these, so the team cannot deploy another until the tower is destroyed.
If the linked power source is disabled or deactivated, the gun is destroyed and the tower is left standing.

ObeliskBeam sets damageType = $ObeliskDamageType instead of the baseDamageType field other lasers use, and $ObeliskDamageType is never defined. The damage type of its hits is not determined from scripts.
The deployer is set as owner for kill credit.
ObeliskPack.source: turretObelisk.cs ObeliskPack::deployShape, ObeliskOfLight::onDestroyed, RealObeliskOfLight, ObeliskPower::onDisabled/onDeactivate; Laser-LightningData.cs ObeliskBeam

ObeliskPowerPack.summary: Deploys the solar-panel power source that an Obelisk of Light must be built next to. One per team.
notes: Placement: within 3 m on a flat surface that is not a building interior, with a clear 1 m spot. There is no enemy-proximity check.
Each power source can feed one Obelisk. It is freed again only when that Obelisk's tower is destroyed.
When the power source is disabled or deactivated, it sets its Obelisk gun's damage to 20, destroying the gun.
On destruction it decrements the team count and makes the standard generator debris blast.
deployShape sets the map name on an undefined variable (%turret), so the power source gets no map name.

JailTurretPack.summary: Jail Turret: a short-range camera turret whose darts teleport enemy players into a jail cell for 30 seconds.
notes: Sold under the Jailing Toyz heading. Uses the shared turret placement rules: any surface within 4 m, no flat-surface or spacing check, blocked near enemy stations, turrets or generators (300 m box).
Fires JailDart, a near-instant rocket with the jail damage type, out to 45 m. It has 10 health.

A jail hit on a player runs jailbolt::damageTarget, which skips the shooter's teammates and non-players. It moves the victim to a Jail Cell pad (from the Jail Package) belonging to any other team and marks them jailed for 30 seconds, during which they cannot deploy anything. With several such pads, it moves them to each in turn and they end at the last one.
If no other team has a Jail Cell deployed, the dart only does its small damage.
Its deployShape calls deployable() without returning the result, so onDeploy's Player::decItemCount never runs: the pack is not used up by deploying, and only the team limit stops repeat deploys.
JailTurretPack.source: turretJail.cs JailTurretPack::deployShape, JailTurret; deployableFuncts.cs deployable(); RocketData.cs JailDart; player.cs Player::onDamage; Laser-LightningData.cs jailbolt::damageTarget; Jail_Package.cs

ArbitorBoxPack.summary: Arbitor Device: a cargo-box deployable that cloaks all friendly players, structures, vehicles and mines around it while it stays enabled. One per team.
notes: Placement: within 3 m on a perfectly level surface (the surface normal must point exactly straight up) with a clear 1 m spot. The terrain check calls CheckDeployTerrain, which this mod never defines, so it never refuses. It does not use the shared turret routine or its enemy-proximity check.

When enabled, it fades out every same-team object in a 150x150x150 m box. Every 6 seconds it re-scans a 200x200x50 m box, cloaking new arrivals and fading back in anything that left, unless that object has its own cloak (cloak pack, boost, gun, plane or device) active.
When disabled or destroyed, everything it cloaked fades back in.
packHackPack.cs lists $Hackable[ArbitorBoxPack], the pack name, instead of the deployed ArbitorBox datablock, so the Hack Gun cannot take it over.

Chaingun.summary: A very fast-firing bullet gun with no spin-up. Each bullet is fast and accurate, and unlike stock Tribes it hurts heavier armor more, not less.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes, the image is single-shot (weaponType 0) with a 0.02 s fire time, so there is no 0.5 s spin-up or 3 s spin-down.

Bullets use the mod's own chaingun damage type instead of the stock bullet type. Its damage scale is 1.0 on Asassin, 1.5 on Mercenary, 2.0 on BoRg and 1.0 on Engineer, the reverse of stock, where heavy armor takes the least.
Because it does not use the bullet damage type, it gets none of the head-shot bonus that the LiL POO rifles get.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it, and it is sold at both inventory and remote stations.
Chaingun.source: wepItem.cs ChaingunImage, Chaingun::onUse; BulletData.cs ChaingunBullet; ArmorData.cs DamageScale; wepFuncts.cs ItemMax

LiLPOOmkiAmmo.summary: Ammunition for the LiL POO mki rifle. It costs nothing, and every armor except the Engineer can carry 10000 rounds.
notes: Dropping it throws out 25 rounds at a time. If 25 or fewer are left and the mki is the weapon in hand, one round is kept back.
Price 0, so buying it uses no team energy.

LiLPOOmki.summary: A rapid-fire sniper rifle with near-instant bullets. A head shot on an enemy makes them explode and deals triple damage.
notes: Fires LiLPOOmkiBullet at 9500 m/s, with a 0.011 s fire time and no reload.

The bullets use the stock bullet damage type. In this mod, Player::onDamage turns any enemy head hit of that type into Player::blowUp plus triple damage, and prints a head-shot message to both players.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it. It is part of the Asassin, Mercenary and BoRg spawn loadouts.

LiLPOOmkiiAmmo.summary: Ammunition for the LiL POO mkii rifle. Every armor except the Engineer can carry 10000 rounds.
notes: Dropping it throws out 25 rounds at a time. If 25 or fewer are left and the mkii is the weapon in hand, one round is kept back.

LiLPOOmkii.summary: The mod's main sniper rifle: a fast-firing rifle with 10000 m/s bullets. Enemy head shots make the target explode for triple damage.
notes: It has its own damage type, which hits Asassins at 1.5x, Mercenaries and Engineers at 1.0x and BoRgs at 0.9x.
Player::onDamage gives this damage type the same enemy head-shot rule as the bullet type: Player::blowUp, triple damage and head-shot messages.

notes: Unlike stock Tribes (0.1 s reload, 0.5 s fire time), reload and fire time are both 0.03 s.
PlasmaBolt has muzzle velocity 600 (stock 55) and damage 1 (stock 0.45), with a radius of 4.
Plasma damage is scaled 0.95x on Asassin, 0.6x on Mercenary, 0.4x on BoRg and 0.45x on Engineer.

notes: Reload and fire time are 0.05 s each, against 0.5 s each in stock Tribes.
Every armor can carry it, the Engineer included. Engineers can hold 350 grenades, more than any other armor.
Grenades still bounce (elasticity 0.45) and deal shrapnel damage.

LiLFFBAmmo.summary: Shells for the LiLForce Field Buster.
notes: Carry limits are 25 for Asassin, 30 for Mercenary, 50 for BoRg and 350 for Engineer.
Dropping it throws out 5 shells at a time.

LiLFFB.summary: A mortar-style launcher that lobs one heavy grenade per second. The grenade's radius damage is far above anything an armor can survive.
notes: Fires LiLFFBShell, a shrapnel grenade with damage 150, a radius of 15 and strong kickback. Every armor's maxDamage is 2.5 or less.
Despite the name, no script treats force fields specially. The shell is simply a high-damage grenade.
The shell can hit its owner once the 250 ms grace period ends (collideWithOwner).
Every armor can carry it, the Engineer included. It is in every spawn loadout except the BoRg's.

ATosserAmmo.summary: Ammunition for the Atom Tosser. Each shot uses one.
notes: Carry limits are 45 for Asassin, 100 for Mercenary and 250 for BoRg, even though only the Asassin can carry the Atom Tosser. Engineers cannot carry it.

ATosser.summary: An Asassin-only launcher that fires a slow rocket shell. When the shell is timed to reach the aim point, it scatters five mortar-type bomblets.
notes: The fire script checks line of sight up to 800 m. If it hits something, the scatter is timed to the distance divided by 180, plus 0.25 s. Otherwise the scatter happens after 2 s.
ScatterBombs spawns five AtomShell2 grenades at the shell's position, each with a random velocity of up to 30 on every axis. They deal mortar damage with a radius of 30.
The original AtomShell is not removed when the bomblets spawn.
Only the Asassin can carry it, and it is sold only at inventory stations, not remote ones.
