FireballAbilityAmmo.summary: Fire Implants, the ammunition for the Fireball Ability.
notes: Carry limits are 200 for Asassin, 250 for Mercenary and 375 for BoRg. Engineers cannot carry it.

FireballAbility.summary: A psionic weapon that shoots fast fireballs. Each one bursts with shrapnel damage over a 15 m radius.
notes: Fires the Fireball bullet at 600 m/s with a 0.05 s reload.
It is listed under the Psionics shop heading. Every armor except the Engineer can carry it.

SmScreenAbilityAmmo.summary: Smoke Implants, the ammunition for the SmokeScreen Ability.
notes: Carry limits are 100 for Asassin, 150 for Mercenary and 200 for BoRg. Engineers cannot carry it.
Dropping it throws out 25 at a time.

SmScreenAbility.summary: A psionic launcher for toxic smoke grenades. Anyone caught in the blast takes extra damage that ignores armor, shields and team.
notes: SmScreen grenades use the smoke damage type with a 5 m radius.

Every smoke hit runs Player::onDamage, which prints a toxic gas warning and adds 0.25 straight to the victim's damage level. This bypasses the armor damage scale, shields and the friendly-fire scale, so it also hurts teammates and the shooter.
The normal 0.2 radius damage is scaled as usual. The Engineer's 0.1 smoke scale only reduces this part.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it.
SmScreenAbility.source: wepPsionics.cs SmScreenAbilityImage; GrenadeData.cs SmScreen; player.cs Player::onDamage

ExSmScreenAbilityAmmo.summary: Lair Implants, the ammunition for the LairWaster.
notes: Carry limits are 25 for Asassin, 75 for Mercenary and 100 for BoRg. Engineers cannot carry it.
Dropping it throws out 25 at a time.

ExSmScreenAbility.summary: A psionic grenade launcher. Its delayed grenade deals overwhelming shrapnel damage in a small radius.
notes: The ExSmScreen grenade's damage is 280 over a 5 m radius, which kills any armor in range. Its liveTime is 6 s, matching the mount message's 'approx. 6 seconds' fuse.
Reload is 0.5 s. Every armor except the Engineer can carry it.

FireScreenAbilityAmmo.summary: FireWall Bombs, the ammunition for the FireWall.
notes: Carry limits are 150 for Asassin, 200 for Mercenary and 275 for BoRg. Engineers cannot carry it.
Dropping it throws out 25 at a time.

FireScreenAbility.summary: A psionic rocket launcher. Its slow fire rockets explode over a wide area, and it can fire every 0.05 s.
notes: FireScreen rockets travel at 80 m/s and deal shrapnel damage with a radius of 20.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it.

SpellAbilityAmmo.summary: SpellHeart, the ammunition for the Spell.
notes: Carry limits are 250 for Asassin, 375 for Mercenary and 500 for BoRg. Engineers cannot carry it.
Dropping it throws out 50 at a time.

SpellAbility.summary: A psionic 'decoy' weapon. It sprays slow projectiles shaped like the female light armor model, and they still do real bullet damage.
notes: SpellAbilityProj uses the lfemale.dts shape, moves at 30 m/s and spreads widely (aimDeflection 0.25). Fire time is 0.1 s.
The projectiles deal the stock bullet damage type, so an enemy head hit triggers the mod's head-shot rule: the target explodes and takes triple damage.
It has no firing sound. Every armor except the Engineer can carry it.
SpellAbility.source: wepPsionics.cs SpellAbilityImage; BulletData.cs SpellAbilityProj; player.cs Player::onDamage

PlasmaCannon2.summary: A hidden companion image for the Plasma Cannon. It is mounted in extra slot 4 and triggered once when a charged shot is released, giving the mortar-gun model and plasma firing sound.
notes: It has no projectile. The shot itself comes from PlasmaCannon::Charge.
It is not sold or shown in the inventory, and no armor has an item max for it.

PlasmaCannon.summary: A charge-up energy cannon. Holding fire converts the wearer's energy into charge, and releasing fires a stronger shot the longer it was held.
notes: Each 0.1 s that fire is held drains 2.5 energy and adds 2 charge, while energy is at least 1 and the charge level is below 3. Charge is capped at the armor's maxEnergy.

Charge levels are 1 at 10 charge, 2 at 35 and 3 at 75. Releasing fires PlasmaCannonBlast with no level, PlasmaCannonBlastlvl1 or lvl2 at those levels, and both PlasmaCannonBlastlvl3 and PlasmaCannonBlastlvl3Add at level 3.
It uses no ammo. Its own damage type hits Mercenaries at 1.5x and BoRgs at 2.0x, but heavy APCs at only 0.5x.
Script bug: the 'Max Charge' message and sound sit in an else-branch that can never run, so level 3 just shows 'Charge Level: 3.'.
Every armor can carry it, the Engineer included. It is the Engineer's default spawn weapon.
PlasmaCannon.source: wepPlasmaCannon.cs PlasmaCannonImage::onFire, PlasmaCannon::Charge, PlasmaCannon::onMount; ArmorData.cs DamageScale; Spawn.cs

LaserRifle.summary: Renamed 'Laser Rifle 6.7'. A rapid-fire sniper laser that, unlike stock Tribes, needs no energy pack and costs almost no energy per shot.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes, onUse just mounts the weapon. There is no energy pack check, and every armor except the Engineer can carry it, not light armor only.
Reload and fire time are 0.03 s, against 0.1 s and 0.5 s in stock. minEnergy is 1 and maxEnergy only 0.5, against 10 and 60 in stock.
sniperLaser's damageConversion is 25, thousands of times the stock 0.007, and its beam time is 0.05 s.
Laser head hits still take 30% extra. Against a BoRg this applies only to hits in the middle quadrants.
It is sold only at inventory stations, not remote ones.
LaserRifle.source: wepEnergyWeps.cs LaserRifleImage, LaserRifle::onUse; Laser-LightningData.cs sniperLaser; player.cs Player::onDamage

TaserRifle.summary: A laser rifle with a long, slow-hitting beam (the 'Vx5 Taser Rifle'). It costs very little energy per shot.
notes: Fires TaserRfLaser, with damageConversion 5.25 and a 0.99 s beam, using the laser damage type, so laser head hits take 30% extra.
minEnergy is 1, maxEnergy 0.5 and reload 0.08 s.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it.

EnergyRifle.summary: The ELF gun, rebuilt into a long, narrow lightning beam that empties a target's energy almost instantly and does real damage.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes, lightningCharge reaches 100 m (stock 40) in a 3-degree cone (stock 35), drains 500 energy per second (stock 60) and deals 2 damage per second (stock 0.06).
Reload is 0.08 s, against 0.2 s in stock. It still uses the stock Lightning::damageTarget.
Electricity damage is scaled 0.7x on Mercenary, and 0.5x on APCs.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it.

BeamOfPain.summary: An ELF-style beam that shoves its target around and makes enemies drop their pack, weapon and flag.
notes: BeamOfPainproj::damageTarget skips teammates unless team damage is at full (1.0). Otherwise it applies an 80-strength impulse built from the shooter's rotation, then 1.25 damage per second and 25 energy drain per second.
Every damage tick on an enemy runs the Beam Of Pain case in Player::onDamage, which drops the victim's mounted pack, weapon and flag.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it.
BeamOfPain.source: wepEnergyWeps.cs BeamOfPainImage; Laser-LightningData.cs BeamOfPainProj, BeamOfPainproj::damageTarget; player.cs Player::onDamage

TargetingLaser.summary: The stock target-painting tool. It is unchanged in function, but only the Engineer can hold it and nothing in the mod hands it out.
notes: Only the Engineer has an item max for it (1).
It is not on any station list (AddToInv 0, 0), not in any spawn loadout and not in the giveall refill, so no script sells or gives it.
It is still a Tool, so it takes no weapon slot. The beam and energy cost are as in stock.
TargetingLaser.source: wepEnergyWeps.cs TargetingLaserImage, TargetingLaser::onUse; wepFuncts.cs AddToInv, ItemMax; Spawn.cs

notes: Carry limits are 500 for Asassin, 750 for Mercenary and 999 for BoRg. Engineers cannot carry it.
The fire script's deductions follow $TG::InfiniteAmmo:TankShredder (off by default), but the extra barrels draw this ammo through their own images.
Dropping it throws out 25 at a time.

TankShredder.summary: A multi-barrel super chaingun. Extra chaingun images are bolted onto the wearer and fire alongside the main gun while the trigger is held.
notes: The main image has no projectile of its own. Its onFire spawns one ShredderBullet and subtracts 0.5 ammo unless $TG::InfiniteAmmo:TankShredder is true.
Mounting it adds TankShredder2 in extra slot 4 at once, and TankShredder3 and 4 in slots 5 and 6 after 1.5 s if it is still in hand.
While fire is held, CheckTankShredder re-triggers slots 4 to 6 every 0.1 s. Those images define their own ShredderBullet projectile and TankShredderAmmo.
ShredderBullet uses the chaingun damage type: 1.0x on Asassin, 1.5x on Mercenary, 2.0x on BoRg.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it. It is the Mercenary's default spawn weapon.
TankShredder.source: wepTankShredder.cs TankShredderImage::onFire, TankShredder::onMount, addMount, CheckTankShredder; BulletData.cs ShredderBullet

TRocketLauncherAmmo.summary: Ammunition for the Tank Rocketgun. Each volley of two rockets uses two.
notes: Carry limits are 150 for Asassin, 200 for Mercenary and 275 for BoRg. Engineers cannot carry it.
No infinite-ammo setting applies.
Dropping it throws out 20 at a time.

TRocketLauncher.summary: A twin rocket launcher. When aimed at a player or flier, it fires two homing missiles and warns the target. Otherwise it fires two straight rockets.
notes: The fire script checks line of sight up to 3500 m. If it hits a Player or Flier, it fires two TankMissile seekers at that object, messages the shooter 'lock acquired' and tells the target a lock was detected.
Admins fire AdminTankMissile instead, with damage 20000. When aimed at something else, God admins fire AdminTankRocket and others fire TankRocket.
Each volley costs 2 ammo.
Three extra launcher models are mounted in slots 4 to 6 and triggered while fire is held. They have no projectile and no fire script, so only the script's two rockets are fired.

Script bugs: the out-of-ammo message uses %client before it is set. When nothing is in line of sight, the admin check reads .isAdmin from the player's name, so admins never get the admin rockets there.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it.
TRocketLauncher.source: wepTankRocket.cs TRocketLauncherImage::onFire, TRocketLauncher::onMount, CheckTRocketLauncher; RocketData.cs TankMissile, AdminTankMissile

MineLauncherAmmo.summary: Ammunition for the MineLauncher. One is used per shot in every mode.
notes: Carry limits are 45 for Asassin, 75 for Mercenary, 100 for BoRg and 15 for Engineer.
Use is skipped when $TG::InfiniteAmmo:MineLauncher is true (off by default).
Dropping it throws out 25 at a time.

MineLauncher.summary: A launcher with five modes, picked in the Tab menu under Weapon Options. The default throws a Claymor mine. The other modes fire flash grenades or shells that burst into flash grenades or mines.
notes: Default mode throws a TG::ClayMorMine from the player's position.
Light Grenade mode fires one EMPgrenshl flash grenade. In Player::onDamage, flash damage empties the victim's energy and whites out their screen.
Burst Mine mode fires a MinerShell. At 3 s it splits into 10 MineFloaters, and each becomes an anti-personnel mine about 2 s later. Then there is a 3 s cooldown.
Tranq mode fires a MinerShell that splits into 10 flash grenades at 3 s. Then there is a 4 s cooldown.

Script bug: the menu sets the Radius Mine mode to 'Radius_Mine', but onFire tests for 'RadiusMine' and would spawn a datablock named Radius_Mine, which does not exist. In that mode nothing is thrown, but ammo is still used.
Script bug: during a cooldown, the burst and tranq modes release the trigger and print 'Re Packing', but they do not return, so a round of ammo is still spent.
Every armor can carry it, the Engineer included.
MineLauncher.source: wepMineLauncher.cs MineLauncherImage::onFire; wepFuncts.cs TG::TossMines, SetMines, SplitExplosion, CoolGun; CharacterOpts.cs processMenuMineLopts

Mortar.summary: Every armor can carry the mortar here. It fires about forty times faster than stock and has four modes from the Tab menu: Default, Nuke, Multi (bunker buster) and Flame.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes, any armor can carry it, the Engineer included, and reload and fire time are 0.05 s each, against 0.5 s and 2.0 s in stock.
Default mode fires MortarShell.

Nuke mode fires MortarShellNuke with a 500 m radius, then has a 5 s cooldown. Its damage type has no armor damage scale, so it does no normal damage. Instead, Player::onDamage fully heals teammates, makes enemies drop their pack, weapon and flag, empties their energy and stops recharge for 10 s.
In Nuke mode, the shooter is unaffected, and so is anyone wearing an Energy Pack (isUnNukable).
Script bug: the nuke case tries to add half of the victim's maxDamage, but reads maxDamage from the player object rather than its datablock, so it adds nothing.
Multi mode fires a MinerShell that splits into five MortarBunkerShells at 3 s, with a 2 s cooldown.
Flame mode fires MortarFlameShell, but refuses to fire if anything is in line of sight within 25 m.
Ammo use is skipped when $TG::InfiniteAmmo:Mortar is true (off by default).
Script bug: shots denied by a Nuke cooldown or the Flame safety still spend a round. A denied Multi shot is free only once per 5 s message window.
Mortar.source: wepMortar.cs MortarImage::onFire; player.cs Player::onDamage; CharacterOpts.cs processMenuMortaropts; packEnergyPack.cs

DoublePlasmaAmmo.summary: Double Plasma Bolts, the ammunition for the Double Plasma. Each shot uses two.
notes: Carry limits are 450 for Asassin, 500 for Mercenary, 999 for BoRg and 350 for Engineer.
Use is skipped when $TG::InfiniteAmmo:DoublePlasma is true (off by default).
Dropping it throws out 50 at a time.

DoublePlasma.summary: A twin-barrel plasma gun. Each shot fires two fast plasma rockets side by side, and it can fire every 0.03 s.
notes: onFire spawns two PlasmaRocket projectiles, one at the muzzle and one offset to the side. These are impact-damage plasma rockets.
A second plasma gun model is mounted in slot 4 one second after the weapon is mounted, and is triggered while fire is held. It has no projectile.
Each shot costs 2 ammo unless $TG::InfiniteAmmo:DoublePlasma is true.
Every armor can carry it, the Engineer included. It is the Asassin's default spawn weapon.

Blaster.summary: An energy pistol every armor can carry. It fires very fast and has a Spredder mode in the Tab menu that fires five bolts at once.
notes: Reload and fire time are 0.03 s, against 0 s and 0.3 s in stock. maxEnergy is 2, against 6 in stock.
Bolts are fired by script. Default mode fires one BlasterBolt. Spredder mode fires five Spredder bolts, each with 0.02 aim deflection.
It is sold only at inventory stations, not remote ones.
Blaster.source: wepBlaster.cs BlasterImage::onFire; BulletData.cs BlasterBolt, Spredder; CharacterOpts.cs processMenuBlasteropts

DiscLauncher.summary: The disc launcher fires far faster discs at a much higher rate than stock. It has Spreader and Invisible modes in the Tab menu.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes, the image is single-shot with no spin-up (weaponType 0, fire time 0, reload 0.05 s), against 1.25 s fire and 0.25 s spin-up in stock.
DiscShell leaves at 600 m/s and accelerates to 800, against 65 to 80 in stock.
Spreader mode fires three DiscSpreader bullets. Invisible mode fires one unseen DiscInvisible.
The fire script never subtracts DiscAmmo, and the $TG::InfiniteAmmo:DiscLauncher setting is never read, so discs are not used up. The launcher still needs at least one disc to fire.
Every armor can carry it, the Engineer included.
DiscLauncher.source: wepDiscLauncher.cs DiscLauncherImage::onFire, DiscShell, DiscSpreader, DiscInvisible; CharacterOpts.cs processMenuDiscopts

JailGun.summary: An ELF-style beam that teleports an enemy into the shooter's team's deployed Jail Cell for 30 seconds. It does nothing if no enemy jail is deployed.
notes: jailbolt::damageTarget ignores non-players and teammates. For each jail pad in the jailports set that does not belong to the target's team, it moves the target there and sets them jailed for 30 s.
On each jailing, it tells the victim the sentence length and sends a message to everyone else.
After 30 s, Jail::JailDoorShape::Sesame moves the prisoner to any opposing release pad within 10 m.
Jailed players cannot deploy items or portals.
The beam does no damage (damagePerSec 0), but drains 60 energy per second. The jail code runs on every beam update while it stays on the target.
Only Mercenaries and BoRgs can carry it, and it is sold only at inventory stations.
JailGun.source: Jail_Weapons.cs JailGunImage; Laser-LightningData.cs jailbolt, jailbolt::damageTarget; Jail_Package.cs Jail::JailDoorShape::Sesame, JailPack::deployshape

JailRifle.summary: A sniper rifle whose darts send the enemy hit to the shooter's team's jail for 30 seconds, using the same code as the Jail Gun.
notes: JailDart uses the jail damage type. Player::onDamage passes it to jailbolt::damageTarget, which teleports enemy players to an opposing jail pad.
That damage type has no armor damage scale, so the dart does no health damage.
Fire time is 0.15 s, minEnergy 10 and maxEnergy 0.01.
Only Asassins and Engineers can carry it, and it is sold only at inventory stations.
JailRifle.source: Jail_Weapons.cs JailRifleImage; RocketData.cs JailDart; player.cs Player::onDamage; Laser-LightningData.cs jailbolt::damageTarget

TankRPGAmmo.summary: RPG Ammo for the Tank RPG.
notes: Carry limits are 50 for Asassin, 75 for Mercenary and 150 for BoRg. Engineers cannot carry it.
The fire script always subtracts one per scripted rocket. No infinite-ammo setting applies.
Dropping it throws out 25 at a time.

TankRPGLauncher.summary: A four-tube RPG rig. The main tube fires an RPG by script, and three extra tubes mounted on the wearer fire their own RPGs while the trigger is held.
notes: onFire subtracts one RPG Ammo and spawns one RPG rocket, which deals shrapnel radius damage.
The extra images TankRPGLauncher2 to 4 are mounted in slots 4, 7 and 6. CheckTankRPGLauncher re-triggers them every 0.1 s. Each defines its own RPG projectile and RPG Ammo.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it. It is the BoRg's default spawn weapon.
TankRPGLauncher.source: wepTankRPG.cs TankRPGLauncherImage::onFire, TankRPGLauncher::onMount, CheckTankRPGLauncher; RocketData.cs RPG

AirStrike.summary: A one-shot targeting device meant to call down bombs on the spot it is aimed at. In this build, the bomb datablock is not loaded, so it produces only sounds and messages.
notes: Firing at a point within 300 m plays explosion sounds and prints a lock-on message. It adds one to the team's airstrike count, limited to 5 per team, and removes the AirStrike from the player.

AirStrike::DropBombs is meant to drop 40 waves of four AirStrikeShell mines, 0.5 s apart. AirStrikeShell is defined only in mineAirStrikeShell.cs, which the loader has commented out, so no bombs appear.
Script bug: the Y offset uses an undefined variable on one branch.

Script bug: DropBombs reschedules itself every 0.5 s forever while the team is within its limit, setting the shooter's AirStrike count to 0 each time. A player who has used one cannot hold another while that player object lives.
The dropship functions Formation3 and MoveShip are never called.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it. It is sold only at inventory stations.
AirStrike.source: AirStrike.cs AirStrikeImage::onFire, AirStrike::DropBombs; TeamItemMax.cs; server[TG].cs LoadMineFiles

DetPackLauncherAmmo.summary: DetPacks for the DetPack Launcher. One is used per throw.
notes: Carry limits are 5 for Mercenary and 10 for BoRg. Asassins and Engineers cannot carry it.
It is sold only at inventory stations. Dropping it throws out 5 at a time.

DetPackLauncher.summary: Throws a timed demolition charge that explodes 20 seconds later in a huge blast. Engineers can disarm it, and Asassins can try, at a risk.
notes: Each shot throws a Suicidebomb2 mine set to the thrower's team. It detonates after 20 s with shrapnel damage 750 over a 200 m radius.
The thrower gets a 20-second warning, then a 5-second countdown and explosion sounds.
Any Engineer, or a God admin, who touches the charge disarms it. This includes the thrower's own team, because the code does not check teams.
An Asassin who touches it has a 20% chance of setting it off, and otherwise disarms it. Mercenaries and BoRgs are ignored.
Script bug: after a failed disarm, the reset is scheduled as '.fuckedup = false:', with a colon instead of a semicolon, so the flag never clears for that client.
Only Mercenaries and BoRgs can carry it.
DetPackLauncher.source: wepDetPackLauncher.cs DetPackLauncherImage::onFire, CheckDetonated; mineSuicide.cs Suicidebomb2, Suicidebomb2::onAdd, Suicidebomb2::onCollision

MineSweeper.summary: An Engineer tool that fires slow energy balls to clear enemy mines. Mines it hits drop a pickup of the matching ammo.
notes: It uses no ammo. onFire spawns MineSweepShell, which deals debug-type radius damage, and triggers the companion MineSweeper2 in slot 4.

An enemy anti-personnel mine hit by it drops a MineAmmo pickup for 4 s and is destroyed. An enemy Claymor drops a TG::ClayMorMineAmmo pickup. A suicide-pack bomb is removed and leaves an Instant Health pickup.
Script bug: the Claymor case sets the mine's damage from a %data variable that is only assigned later in the function, so the Claymor is not destroyed by that line.
Players have no damage scale for the debug type, so the shell does not hurt them.
Only the Engineer can carry it. It is sold only at inventory stations and is in the Engineer's spawn loadout.
MineSweeper.source: wepDebug.cs MineSweeperImage::onFire, MineSweeper::onMount; mineAnti-Personel.cs AntipersonelMine::onDamage; mineClaymor.cs TG::ClayMorMine::onDamage; mineSuicide.cs Suicidebomb::onDamage

MineSweeper2.summary: A hidden companion image for the Mine Sweeper. It is mounted in slot 4 to show a second launcher model and plays its fire effect when the Mine Sweeper fires.
notes: It has no projectile. It is not shown in the inventory, and no armor has an item max for it.

NDiscAmmo.summary: Ammunition for the hidden Quad Disc.
notes: It is not on any station list. The only way to get it is to buy the Quad Disc itself, which fills it to the armor's maximum.
Carry limits are 250 for Asassin, 325 for Mercenary and 800 for BoRg. No Engineer max is set.

NDisc.summary: The hidden Quad Disc: a launcher with four disc barrels mounted around the wearer. It fires discs two at a time in alternating pairs.
notes: Typing QUADDISC in chat with $TG::GiveallOn set runs buyItem for it, then equips it.

buyItem only succeeds if the item is on the client's shopping list, or server or test cheats are on, or the client is in spawn buying. NDisc is never added to a station list, so the chat word alone normally fails.
The four disc models NDisc1 to 4 are mounted in slots 4 to 7.
The first shot fires two NDiscShell discs from an offset position, the second 0.35 s later, and spends no ammo. The next shot fires two from the muzzle, 0.45 s apart, and spends 2 ammo.
It is not in the next/previous weapon cycle, so it can only be selected by using the item directly.
Every armor except the Engineer can carry it.
NDisc.source: dfjhsbdfsdf.cs NDiscImage::onFire, NDisc::onMount, NDisc::onDrop; comchat.cs; ItemFuncts.cs buyItem; RocketData.cs NDiscShell

NDisc1.summary: One of the four hidden disc models of the Quad Disc. It is mounted in slot 4 and triggered for its fire effect when the Quad Disc fires.
notes: It has no projectile and is not shown in the inventory. The discs themselves are spawned by NDiscImage::onFire.

EnergyPack.summary: Renamed Engineer Pack. Unlike stock Tribes' Energy Pack it is a combat-engineering pack only the Engineer can carry: activating it equips a Repair Gun in the weapon slot and turns on a very strong energy shield plus immunity to nuclear damage.
notes: Only the Engineer armor can carry it; it is the Engineer's default pack at spawn.

Activating sets the wearer's shield strength to 1.0, so each point of energy absorbs a full point of damage (stock Shield Pack: 0.012). With the Engineer's large energy pool this blocks almost everything until energy runs out.
While active the wearer is also flagged un-nukable: nuclear damage only prints 'Nuke Shield Enabled' and does nothing.
The pack still has a negative energy cost, so it adds energy while running, as the stock Energy Pack did.
Using the pack again while it is active swaps the tool between the Repair Gun and the Hack Gun.
The Repair Gun and Hack Gun switch the pack off when they are unmounted and on when mounted, so putting the gun away (switching weapons) also drops the shield.

EnergyPack::onActivate always mounts the Repair Gun, and swapping guns re-triggers the pack through those mount handlers, so a switch to the Hack Gun can be bounced back to the Repair Gun. The actual in-game result is not determined from scripts.
No weapon script checks for it, so unlike stock Tribes it is not tied to the laser rifle.
EnergyPack.source: packEnergyPack.cs EnergyPack::onUse, EnergyPack::onActivate, EnergyPack::onDeactivate; packRepairPack.cs RepairGun::onMount/onUnmount; packHackPack.cs HackGun::onMount/onUnmount; player.cs Player::onDamage; packFuncts.cs ItemMax

RepairGun.summary: A repair beam weapon. It is the gun handed out by the Repair Pack (standard setting) and the Engineer Pack, and the Engineer can also buy it on its own. It reaches 50 m and repairs much faster than the stock repair gun.
notes: Repairs others at a rate of 1.5 and the wielder at 1.25, against 0.1 and 0.05 for the stock repair gun.
Pointing it at an enemy object (not a player) is refused: the wielder gets an insult and every player sees a message that they tried to betray their team. Enemy players can still be repaired.
Finishing a repair on a teammate or friendly object (beam released with the target at full health) gives 1 point of score.
Mounting it triggers the backpack slot and unmounting it releases it, which is what switches the Engineer Pack on and off.
As a standalone purchase only the Engineer can carry it.
RepairGun.source: packRepairPack.cs RepairBolt::onAcquire, RepairBolt::onRelease, RepairBolt::checkDone, RepairGun::onMount/onUnmount/onUse; packFuncts.cs ItemMax

RepairRifle.summary: The 'Advanced Repair Gun': a long-range repair beam on a sniper-rifle model, given by the Repair Pack when the player picks the advanced option in the pack options menu. It repairs almost instantly from up to 1000 m.
notes: Selected through the Repair Pack Options menu (Advanced Repair Gun); with that setting, using an equipped Repair Pack mounts the Repair Rifle instead of the Repair Gun.
Adds 350 to the target's auto-repair rate, so targets heal essentially at once.
Unlike the Repair Gun it has no team check: it will repair enemy players and enemy objects, and it never awards score.
It is not sold separately; it only comes from the Repair Pack.

RepairPack.summary: Gives the wearer a repair beam. Using the pack while worn equips either the Repair Gun or, if the player chose the advanced option, the Repair Rifle. Every armor except the Engineer can carry it, and it is the default pack for the other three classes.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes, the gun it gives reaches 50 m (Repair Gun) or 1000 m (Repair Rifle) and repairs far faster; see those items.
The Engineer cannot carry a Repair Pack; the Engineer Pack replaces it.
Unmounting the pack removes either repair gun from the weapon slot.
Dropping the pack only checks for the Repair Gun; a mounted Repair Rifle is cleared by the unmount handler instead.
The pack itself costs almost no energy while on.
RepairPack.source: packRepairPack.cs RepairPack::onUse, RepairPack::onUnmount, RepairPack::onDrop; packFuncts.cs ItemMax; Spawn.cs SpawnBuyList

HackPack.summary: Gives the wearer a Hack Gun beam that converts enemy deployables, turrets and stations to the wearer's team for 25 seconds. Aimed at a friendly object it makes that object hack-proof for 25 seconds instead.
notes: Carried by the Mercenary and the Engineer (the Engineer also gets the Hack Gun through the Engineer Pack).
Using the pack while worn mounts the Hack Gun.
Hacking takes the beam held on the target for 15 checks spaced 0.5 s apart (about 7.5 s); letting go or losing the target interrupts it and resets the progress.

Only objects on a fixed list can be hacked, including inventory, ammo and command stations, stock and mod turrets (plasma, rocket, mortar, indoor, camera, laser, ELF, taser), the Deployable Base and its doors, blast walls, force field floors, shock floors, the Arbitor device, the air base and the portable hole. Force field doors, teleport pads and holograms cannot be hacked.
A hacked object switches to the hacker's team and goes back to its original team 25 seconds later. Hacking an already hacked object switches it again.
Every successful hack also repairs the target by 0.99, because the check guarding that repair reads a variable that is never set.
Beaming a friendly object gives it a firewall for 25 seconds; a firewalled object cannot be hacked.
HackPack.source: packHackPack.cs HackPack::onUse/onUnmount/onDrop, HackBolt::onAcquire/onRelease, CheckHackStatus, HackPack::UnHack, SetupHackList; packFuncts.cs ItemMax

BoRgItem1.summary: A cosmetic part of the BattlePack Advanced: a mortar-gun model mounted on the wearer's side while the BattlePack (BoRgDevice) is worn. It has no functions of its own.
notes: Mounted automatically into an extra slot when the BattlePack is mounted and removed when it is unmounted.
When the BattlePack fires, this slot is triggered too, but it has no projectile; the shots come from the BattlePack itself.
It is not sold on its own, and dropping the BattlePack sets its count to 0.

BoRgItem2.summary: A cosmetic part of the BattlePack Advanced: a sensor-jammer pack model mounted in an extra slot while the BattlePack (BoRgDevice) is worn. It has no functions of its own.
notes: Mounted automatically when the BattlePack is mounted and removed when it is unmounted.
The BattlePack's sensor suppression comes from BoRgDevice::onMount, not from this item.
It is not sold on its own, and dropping the BattlePack sets its count to 0.

BoRgDevice.summary: The BattlePack: a weapon pack for the Mercenary and the BoRg. Wearing it gives a light shield and some sensor suppression and adds two side-mounted parts; activating the pack fires a pair of rockets from the wearer's muzzle.
notes: Carried only by the Mercenary and BoRg armors.
While mounted the wearer gets shield strength 0.008 and sensor suppression 3; both are cleared when it is taken off.
Each activation fires two NukeTurret rockets (missile damage), one from the muzzle and one offset to the side. Super admins fire two AdminTankRocket shots instead.
Mounting it also mounts BoRgItem1 and BoRgItem2 as visual parts; dropping it removes them from the inventory.
On mount it triggers slot 2, which is the flag slot rather than the backpack slot.
The pack can only be dropped when the weapon slot is not firing or reloading.
BoRgDevice.source: packBoRgPack.cs BoRgDevice::onMount/onUnmount/onDrop, BoRgDeviceImage::onActivate/onDeactivate; RocketData.cs NukeTurret; packFuncts.cs ItemMax

HiderPack.summary: The Morph Pack hides the wearer for up to 15 seconds. The player's body is moved far below the map and replaced by a decoy (an electrical beam, a flag stand and an upside-down flag stand) at their position, while the player watches it from an orbiting camera.
notes: Carried by every armor except the BoRg.
The pack switches itself off after 15 seconds; pressing jump returns earlier. Either way the player is put back where they started.

A living player whose team differs from the decoy stand's who touches it is set on fire repeatedly (a FireScreen projectile every 0.2 s) until they die, and a rocket that hits it is destroyed. The stand is never assigned a team, so the check compares against its default team and teammates of the hider are not protected by it. The stand cannot be damaged.

Activating it with a flag is meant to drop the flag, but the script passes the flag slot number to Player::dropItem instead of the flag item, and the 'Flag Dropped' message goes to an unset client variable.
Inventory and menus are locked while it is active.
HiderPack::holdPlayer, a loop that would hold the hidden body still, is never called.
HiderPack.source: packHider.cs HiderPackImage::onActivate/onDeactivate, HiderStand::onCollision/onDamage; observer.cs Observer::jump; AdminFunctions.cs BurnUp

CloakingDevice.summary: Makes the wearer fade out of view and hides them from sensors while the pack is on.
notes: Carried by every armor except the BoRg.
Turning it on fades the wearer out and sets sensor suppression to 5; turning it off fades them back in and sets suppression to 0.
It costs almost no energy while on (0.1 per second).

ShieldPack.summary: Projects an energy shield that absorbs damage out of the wearer's energy, like stock Tribes, but weaker per point of energy and almost free to keep running.
notes: Each point of energy absorbs 0.009 damage (0.00675 against shrapnel and mortars), against 0.012 in stock Tribes.
If a hit is larger than the energy can absorb, energy drops to 0 and the rest goes through.
Running cost is 0.1 energy per second against 9 in stock Tribes; it still needs 4 energy to switch on.
Every armor can carry it.

SensorJammerPack.summary: Renamed StealthShield Pack. Unlike the stock Sensor Jammer it combines sensor jamming with a shield that is stronger than the mod's Shield Pack.
notes: While on, the wearer gets shield strength 0.025 (the Shield Pack gives 0.009) and sensor suppression 3.
Stock Tribes added 20 to the wearer's sensor suppression; this pack sets it to 3 and resets it to 0 when switched off, overriding any other suppression.
Running cost is 0.1 energy per second against 10 in stock Tribes.
Carried by every armor except the BoRg.

SuicidePack.summary: The Suicide DetPack. Using it while worn throws a large bomb that explodes 20 seconds later with a very large, very strong shrapnel blast.
notes: Every armor can carry one.
The bomb (Suicidebomb2) is lobbed a short way and the wearer is told it will self-destruct in 20 seconds.

A male Asassin (larmor) or an Engineer of either team who touches the bomb tries to disarm it. Engineers and God admins always succeed. Other male Asassins succeed 80% of the time; otherwise the bomb goes off at once. Female Asassins and other armors cannot disarm it.
The bomb is given no team, so the blast hits everyone in range, including the thrower.
SuicidePack::deployShape returns no value, so onDeploy never removes the pack from the inventory; the pack is only unmounted and can be used again.
It is also a dead-man switch: if the wearer dies with it mounted, a bomb is thrown from the body and a countdown is shown to the dead player before it goes off 20 seconds later.
SuicidePack::onUnmount schedules deleteObject on its second argument, which the engine passes as the mount slot, not on the deployed bomb.

instantHealth.summary: Instant Health: a one-use kit that repairs 0.99 damage, and also a pickup that fully heals any teammate who touches it.
notes: Using it from the inventory repairs 0.99 damage, the same as this mod's Repair Kit.
Carry limits: 3 for the Asassin, 5 for the Mercenary, 7 for the BoRg; the Engineer has no allowance.
As a pickup, a player of the item's team who touches it is repaired by their armor's full maxDamage. The pickup is not removed when used.

It is not on any station's buy list. Scripts drop one only when a Suicidebomb mine is hit with debug (Mine Sweeper) damage, and nothing in the scripts creates a Suicidebomb, so in practice it is not obtainable.

LightArmor.summary: Renamed Asassin: the light class. It carries the most weapons and is fast, with the lowest health. Male and female versions differ: the female suit has less health, fewer weapon slots and a weaker jump.
notes: Male Asassins can hold 20 weapons and female Asassins 15, against 3 for stock light armor.
The female suit (lfemale) has maxDamage 0.66 against 0.99 for the male (larmor).

Cannot carry most deployables (inventory, ammo and other stations, force fields, blast walls, teleporters, jail), the BattlePack, Hack Pack, Ammo Pack, DetPack Launcher or Jail Gun. Asassin-only items are the Atom Tosser and, shared with the Engineer, the Jail Rifle and Cloak Droid.
Unlike stock light armor it takes reduced shrapnel (0.7), bullet (0.8) and landing (0.1) damage, but 1.5 times LiL POO mkii damage.
Only a male Asassin (or an Engineer) can try to disarm a Suicide DetPack, with a 20% chance of setting it off.
A God admin wearing it knocks back and damages enemies they touch, and fully heals and adds energy to teammates they touch.
Default spawn loadout: Repair Pack, mines, Beacons, Grenades, Tunneler, Repair Kit and a large weapon set, starting with the Double Plasma.
LightArmor.source: ArmorLight.cs larmor/lfemale, larmor::onCollision, lfemale::onCollision; ArmorData.cs DamageScale; wepFuncts.cs, packFuncts.cs, deployableFuncts.cs ItemMax; Spawn.cs SpawnBuyList; mineSuicide.cs Suicidebomb2::onCollision

MediumArmor.summary: Renamed Mercenary: the mid-weight class. It has more health than the Asassin, can carry the deployables, the BattlePack and the Hack Pack, but cannot crouch and moves a little slower.
notes: Holds 12 weapons, against 4 for stock medium armor.
Neither the male nor the female suit can crouch.
Takes 1.5 times plasma cannon and chaingun damage, 0.6 plasma, 0.5 shrapnel and 0.7 from most other types, including electricity, mines and explosions.

Can carry the inventory and ammo stations, force fields, blast walls, teleporters and other deployables, plus the BattlePack, Hack Pack and Ammo Pack. Cannot carry Engineer-only items or the Atom Tosser, Jail Rifle or Cloak Droid.
Default spawn loadout: Repair Pack, mines, Beacons, Grenades, Repair Kit and a weapon set, starting with the Tank Shredder.
MediumArmor.source: ArmorMedium.cs marmor/mfemale; ArmorData.cs DamageScale; wepFuncts.cs, packFuncts.cs, deployableFuncts.cs ItemMax; Spawn.cs SpawnBuyList

EnginArmor.summary: The Engineer: a new class with one suit for both genders. It repairs damaged friendly equipment just by touching it, gets the Engineer Pack, and has a very large energy pool, but it is barred from most heavy weapons.
notes: Holds 10 weapons. Male and female players both get the same Earmor suit (medium-armor model).
Touching a damaged friendly object (not a player) repairs it completely.
Engineer-only items: the Engineer Pack, the standalone Repair Gun, the Mine Sweeper and the Targeting Laser. The Engineer also carries the Hack Pack, Jail Rifle and Cloak Droid.

Cannot carry the Repair Pack, BattlePack, Repair Kit, Radius Mine, LiLBoost, Tunneler, Land Camo or Instant Health, nor most of the mod's heavy weapons and abilities (tank rocket and RPG launchers, Tank Shredder, DetPack Launcher, the abilities, laser, taser and ELF rifles, Beam of Pain, LiL POO guns, chaingun, plasma gun, air strike).
Its default spawn list includes a Repair Kit, but the Engineer has no Repair Kit allowance, so the kit is not given.
Takes 2.5 times flame damage but only 0.1 impact, landing and smoke damage, 0.45 plasma and 0.5 bullet, laser, shrapnel and mine damage.
Engineer mines are thrown much harder and Beacons produce a different boost blast; see Mine and Beacon.
Default spawn loadout: Engineer Pack, mines, Beacons, Grenades, Mine Launcher, Mine Sweeper, Mortar, LiLForce Field Buster, DetPack Launcher and Plasma Cannon.
EnginArmor.source: ArmorEngineer.cs Earmor, Earmor::onCollision; item.cs $ArmorType; ArmorData.cs DamageScale; wepFuncts.cs, packFuncts.cs ItemMax; Spawn.cs SpawnBuyList

HeavyArmor.summary: Renamed BoRg: the heavy class, with the most health and the largest ammo limits. It resists most damage types but is especially vulnerable to plasma cannons and chainguns, and it cannot use the stealth packs.
notes: Holds 10 weapons, against 5 for stock heavy armor. It cannot crouch.
Takes 2.0 times plasma cannon and chaingun damage, but only 0.4 plasma and shrapnel and 0.6 bullet, explosion, missile, laser, mortar and blaster damage.
Cannot carry the StealthShield Pack, Cloaking Device, Hack Pack or Morph Pack, nor Engineer-only items. It can carry the BattlePack.
As in stock Tribes, laser head shots only get the 30% bonus on the centre of the head.
Default spawn loadout: Repair Pack, mines, Beacons, Grenades, Repair Kit, DetPack Launcher and a weapon set, starting with the Tank RPG launcher.
HeavyArmor.source: ArmorHeavy.cs harmor; ArmorData.cs DamageScale; player.cs Player::onDamage; wepFuncts.cs, packFuncts.cs ItemMax; Spawn.cs SpawnBuyList

RepairKit.summary: A one-use kit that repairs 0.99 damage, almost a full heal, against 0.2 in stock Tribes.
notes: Carry limits: 3 for the Asassin, 5 for the Mercenary, 7 for the BoRg (stock: 1 for everyone). The Engineer has no allowance and cannot buy or hold one.
Always used up: the $TG::InfiniteAmmo:RepairKit setting is never read by any script.

MineAmmo.summary: Thrown mines that arm once they come to rest and explode when an enemy touches them. Unlike stock Tribes they deal EMP damage, and that damage only affects players on the thrower's own team.
notes: Mines only trigger for enemy players, vehicles and moving objects, where stock mines had no team check.

The blast uses the EMP damage type. Player::onDamage ignores EMP damage when the victim and the source are on different teams, so the enemy who sets the mine off takes knockback but no damage. Teammates in the blast, and the thrower, lose all energy and drop their pack, weapon and flag; teammates then take damage scaled by the server's team damage setting, the thrower takes it in full.
Mines ignore EMP damage themselves. A hit from an enemy's Mine Sweeper (debug damage) defuses the mine and leaves a MineAmmo pickup for 4 seconds.
The Engineer throws mines with a throw animation and a 0.8 s delay, at 55 times throw strength against 15 for other armors.

Unless $TG::InfiniteAmmo:Mine is on (off by default), each use takes a mine even during the 0.5 s throw cooldown when nothing is thrown. The Engineer's throw takes a second mine on top of that, so an Engineer uses two per throw.
Walking over a loose MineAmmo item picks up one mine if below the carry limit.
A mine that lands on another mine detonates.
Carry limits: Asassin 10, Mercenary 20, Engineer 25, BoRg 35.
MineAmmo.source: item.cs MineAmmo::onUse, MineAmmo::onCollision; mineAnti-Personel.cs AntipersonelMine::onCollision/deployCheck/onDamage; player.cs Player::onDamage; TribalPrefs.cs

RadiusMineAmmo.summary: A single thrown Radius Mine (shown with a flag model) that arms at rest and goes off when an enemy comes within its much wider trigger radius.
notes: One per armor; the Engineer cannot carry it.

Its trigger radius is 10, against 1 for the standard mine. Once armed, any collision with an object of a different team sets it off: the type test includes a comparison of the mine's own datablock with RadiusMine, which is always true.
Deals mine damage over a 20 m radius.
Like other mines it detonates if it lands on another mine, and it is destroyed after taking enough damage (mine damage counts at a quarter).
Always used up when thrown; it ignores the infinite-ammo settings.
Its destroy handler lowers a team count that the throw never raises.

Grenade.summary: In Tribal God the Grenade is an air brake, not a hand grenade. Using it cuts the player's current velocity to one sixth.
notes: Nothing is thrown: Grenade::onUse just scales the user's velocity down by 6 and prints 'AirBrake Used.'
There is no throw cooldown.
The infinite-ammo check is inverted: a Grenade is used up only when $TG::InfiniteAmmo:Grens is true (the default), and becomes free when it is set to false.
Carry limits: Asassin 100, Mercenary 125, Engineer and BoRg 250.

FlashGrenade.summary: A thrown flash grenade that goes off after 2 seconds, whiting out the screens of players in a large radius and wiping their energy.
notes: Uses the flash damage type over a 30 m radius. Each player hit gets a heavy screen flash, energy set to 0 and a recharge rate of 8, plus a small amount of damage.
There is no team check, so teammates and the thrower are affected too.
Thrown more softly than mines (9 times throw strength), with a 0.5 s cooldown; always used up.
Carry limits: Asassin 40, Mercenary 65, Engineer and BoRg 90.
FlashGrenade.source: item.cs FlashGrenade::onUse; mineGrenades.cs Flash, Flash::onAdd; player.cs Player::onDamage

LiLBoostammo.summary: LiLBoost: a smaller version of the Beacon speed boost. It drops a zero-damage mine at the player's feet whose blast gives a light push.
notes: The mine does no damage; its kickback is about a fifth of the Beacon boost's over an 8 m radius.
Its class is Mine, which has no fuse or contact handler in this mod, so what sets it off is not determined from scripts; it can be detonated by damage.
Uses the grenade setting rather than the boost setting: it is used up only when $TG::InfiniteAmmo:Grens is false, so it is free by default.
0.6 s between uses. The Engineer cannot carry it; every other armor can hold 35.
LiLBoostammo.source: item.cs LiLBoostammo::onUse; Mine.cs lilBoost, lilBoost::onDamage; TribalPrefs.cs

RepairPatch.summary: A repair pickup found lying in missions. Running over it heals 0.5 damage if the player is hurt, against 0.125 in stock Tribes.
notes: Used from the inventory it still heals only 0.1.
The patch respawns after being picked up.

cactusPack.summary: Land Camo: a backpack that mounts a cactus model on the wearer as a disguise. It has no scripted effect beyond the model.
notes: It defines no functions of its own; it uses the generic backpack behavior.
The cactus is mounted low on the back, so it reaches down around the wearer.
One per armor, except the Engineer, who cannot carry it. Up to 10 per team.
cactusPack.source: item.cs cactusPack, cactuspackImage; packFuncts.cs Backpack::onUse; TeamItemMax.cs

Tunneler.summary: A reusable teleporter. Using it moves the player instantly to the point their view hits, up to 225 m away.
notes: Never used up.
The script does not test whether the line-of-sight check hit anything; where the player ends up when nothing is in range is not determined from scripts.
One per armor, except the Engineer, who cannot carry it. It is part of the Asassin's default spawn loadout.

Beacon.summary: In Tribal God the Beacon is a speed boost, not a target marker. Using it drops a zero-damage mine at the player's feet whose blast throws them along.
notes: The boost mine has strong kickback over a 20 m radius and deals no damage, so it pushes any nearby player.
Engineers get an EngineerBoost mine with its own explosion effect; it is otherwise the same as everyone else's Boost.
The mines use the Handgrenade class, whose onAdd sets them off 2 seconds after they are dropped; damaging one sets it off at once.
0.2 s between uses. Used up only when $TG::InfiniteAmmo:Boosts is false; it is free by default.
Carry limits: Asassin 100, Mercenary 175, Engineer 150, BoRg 250.
Beacon.source: itemBoost.cs Beacon::onUse, ItemMax; Mine.cs Boost, EngineerBoost, Boost::onDamage, EngineerBoost::onDamage; mineGrenades.cs Handgrenade::onAdd; TribalPrefs.cs
